name: Rocket Mortar
perkDesc: Fires in an arced trajectory at a designated area on the ground.
strengths: Arced fire reaches 225m; 4m AoE splash absorbs near-misses; damage on impact with no fuse delay.
weaknesses: 46m minimum range rules out close/mid fights; slow projectile telegraphs the arc; long reload with small magazine.
reasoning: Budget artillery entry. Arced bombardment from safety, but Ground Target adds nothing beyond the base class mechanic. Outclassed by the Fuse Mortar at every shared energy tier.

name: Fuse Mortar
perkDesc: Scatters motion-sensitive Bombs over a large area that explode when enemies approach. The Bombs detonate instantly if they hit a Mech directly. If no enemies trigger the fuse, they will explode after a short time.
strengths: Trip Hazard scatters bombs — persistent area denial; bombs detonate on direct mech contact; same 225m reach as Rocket Mortar.
weaknesses: 45m minimum range rules out close fights; detonation delay lets aware enemies vacate; scatter can spread damage rather than concentrate it.
reasoning: Trip Hazard converts each shot into a multi-bomb scatter — four salvos can deny an entire objective zone. Higher DPS and larger blast radius than the Rocket Mortar make it the clear superior at every shared energy tier.

name: Shotgun
perkDesc: Shots fire in a cone, making them good at hitting fast targets or at short range.
strengths: Wide hit cone forgives poor aim; accessible at just 2 energy.
weaknesses: Lowest DPS in CQ; Uncommon rarity caps damage; small magazine with slow reload.
reasoning: Budget placeholder. Fills a slot cheaply at 2 energy but damage ceiling is too low to compete with any Epic or Legendary CQ option. Use only when energy is genuinely exhausted.

name: Fragment Gun
perkDesc: Shots fire in a cone, making them good at hitting fast targets or at short range.
strengths: Highest damage per shot of any Rare CQ weapon; wide hit cone connects reliably against mobile targets; available across five energy tiers.
weaknesses: 13m optimal range demands near point-blank positioning; punishes every miss; small magazine.
reasoning: Dependable Rare with serious per-shot damage. The 13m optimal range is the defining constraint — demands extreme aggression. Outperformed by all Epic/Legendary CQ options but solid when energy budget is tight.

name: Arc Torrent
perkDesc: Applies a Shock Effect that destabilizes the crosshair of the target.
strengths: High Voltage Shock destabilizes aim rapidly.
weaknesses: Worst dmgPerEnergy of all CQ weapons; one of the worst reloads in the game; raw damage relies entirely on Shock utility.
reasoning: CQ utility outlier — Shocks enemies from outside their comfortable fight-back range. One of the worst reloads in the game. Strong in coordinated play; weak solo.

name: Ember Gun
perkDesc: Fires twice, applying Weaken. Fast reload for a brutal follow-up.
strengths: Weaken on both shots boosts allied damage; fast reload creates near-constant burst cycling; strong DPS at max rank.
weaknesses: Tiny 2-shot magazine punishes every miss; hit cone narrows sharply at max rank; contributes more in team play than solo.
reasoning: Team-oriented burst weapon. Twin Shots applies Weaken on both hits for allied follow-up damage. Fast reload stays aggressive but the tiny magazine is punishing solo — punches above its numbers in coordinated play, falls short of Howler and Repeater in isolation.

name: Howler
perkDesc: Fires a sound blast that penetrates through enemies. Applies Shock, impairing aim.
strengths: Highest DPS in CQ; Cacophony penetrates through multiple enemies for full damage each; Shock on every hit; longest max range in CQ.
weaknesses: Penetration wasted in 1v1 fights; requires directional aim; 19m optimal range demands aggressive positioning.
reasoning: Undisputed CQ benchmark. Cacophony staggers entire formations while dealing full damage to each target. No other CQ weapon combines raw output, crowd control, and penetration at this level.

name: Repeater
perkDesc: High damage with a recharging magazine for near-constant close-range fire.
strengths: Highest fire rate in CQ; recharging magazine eliminates reload downtime; ~15% Double Damage Chance adds burst spikes; wide hit cone.
weaknesses: 15m optimal and max range demand constant point-blank aggression; loses all value when a target creates distance.
reasoning: Close-range spray weapon. Recharging magazine means near-endless fire in the pocket, with random double-damage spikes. Second only to Howler in CQ — requires a fast mech to stay close.

name: Revoker
perkDesc: Fires a dart that deals damage outbound and on the return. Reloads almost instantly after the dart returns.
strengths: Outbound hit + 2× back damage on return = 3× listed damage per throw; near-instant reload after dart return; self-returning dart makes hits reliable.
weaknesses: Single dart; return trip misses if target moves out of path before it returns; cycle rate drops at longer range.
reasoning: Most mechanically unique CQ weapon. Every dart deals full outbound damage then strikes from behind on return for 2× (back damage bonus), tripling total output per throw. Near-instant reload at point-blank puts cycle rate among the fastest in category. Exceptional vs stationary targets; needs positioning discipline against highly mobile ones.

name: Pod Gun
perkDesc: Fires bombs which stick to surfaces and detonate after a short delay.
strengths: 300m max range — far beyond any counter-fire; largest blast radius in barrage; Sticky Bombs pre-place area denial; ~25% Double Damage Chance.
weaknesses: Lowest damage per shot in category — both Epics outclass it in raw output; Sticky Bombs detonation delay lets mobile targets escape; worst dmgPerEnergy of the three.
reasoning: Range and control specialist — A-tier through utility, not damage. 300m reach with Sticky Bombs turns objectives into denial zones no counter-fire can match. Underperforms against open-field mobile targets but uniquely powerful in any objective-based play.

name: Cryo Launcher
perkDesc: Sustained fire applies a Stasis Effect that dramatically slows the target.
strengths: Stasis locks targets for follow-up rounds, multiplying effective output; second-highest per-shot damage in category; 95m range stays outside most counter-fire.
weaknesses: Stasis requires sustained fire — fast targets can disengage before it applies; slightly lower output than Nade Launcher at max rank.
reasoning: CC anchor of the barrage category. Stasis-locked targets cannot sprint from follow-up rounds, closing the DPS gap with the Nade Launcher through utility. Opens coordinated burst windows no other barrage weapon can create.

name: Nade Launcher
perkDesc: Launch trajectory makes it possible to arc grenades over obstacles.
strengths: Highest damage per shot in barrage; fire rate and reload scale with rank; highest DPM of the three; Incoming arc clears walls and terrain.
weaknesses: 80m max range is shortest of the three; heavily rank-dependent at low levels; no CC perk against mobile targets.
reasoning: Pure damage pick. At max rank it hits hardest per shot while matching the Cryo Launcher on cycle speed. Incoming adds a positional advantage when obstacles are present. Range ceiling is the only real constraint — at max rank it is the highest-damage barrage option.

name: Bouncecritter
perkDesc: Deals damage to a secondary enemy upon hitting the first one, if unobstructed; Recharges a shot on double damage
strengths: Neglible
weaknesses: Very weak base damage; long reload; no radius if the shot does not hit, so makes it ineffective against mechs in cover.
reasoning: The damage is quite underwhelming, the reload is rather long for its damage, and the perk is rarely ever useful. Even if you manage to bounce back, the damage is practically useless.

name: Chain Gun
perkDesc: This Weapon's Fire Rate increases over time when the trigger is held.
strengths: Build Up reaches full fire rate with sustained trigger; large magazine for extended windows; ~25% Double Damage Chance; 110m max range; now competitive per-shot damage.
weaknesses: Ramp-up punishes short bursts; significant reload; no utility perk unlike Suppressor.
reasoning: The +25% damage buff pushes Chain Gun past Dreadshot's per-energy output (~1,119) and into A-tier. Once fully spun up, sustained DPS is among the highest in the heavy category. The ramp-up requirement and lack of utility still keep it behind Suppressor's S-tier Damage Drain, but it is no longer the weakest heavy option.

name: Minigun
perkDesc: Provides a continuous barrage of suppressing fire.
strengths: 200-round magazine — nearly 38s of fire; highest total DPM in category (267,200); 130m range; volume alone forces enemies into cover.
weaknesses: Longest reload in the game; spin-up delay before first shot; widest hit cone in category; halved turn speed while firing requires pre-aiming.
reasoning: Commitment weapon. Unmatched sustained volume, but the spin-up delay, brutal reload, wide hit cone, and halved turn speed demand a pre-aimed stationary target. Exceptional in fixed defensive corridors; crippled in dynamic fights.

name: Hellfire
perkDesc: Releases a sustained stream of fire. Applies the Burn Effect, which deals continuous damage to its target.
strengths: Highest sustained DPS in category at close range; Burn DoT stacks beyond visible fire rate; tight hit cone; fast reload.
weaknesses: 40m hard range cap — useless beyond that; forces close-range trades against enemies at peak damage too; fast mechs can escape before Burn DoT completes.
reasoning: Highest-output heavy weapon within its 40m envelope. Burn DoT stacks produce numbers nothing else in class matches up close. Devastating on gap-closing mechs; a liability on slow ones.

name: Dreadshot
perkDesc: Each shot deals a massive amount of Damage to the target.
strengths: Highest damage per shot in heavy duty; longest range in class; high accuracy and fast projectile speed; ~25% Double Damage Chance.
weaknesses: Slowest fire rate in category — each miss is costly; lower DPM than Minigun and Hellfire within their optimal conditions.
reasoning: Relatively underwhelming weapon overall. Needs large exposures to deal any considerable amount of damage, much better alternatives exist.

name: Suppressor
perkDesc: Projectiles apply Damage Drain, reducing the target's damage output. Stacks up to 6 times.
strengths: Damage Drain stacks to 40% damage reduction; highest per-shot damage in class; splash radius on every shot; highest dmgPerEnergy in heavy duty.
weaknesses: Full stack takes ~9.5s — fast mechs can disengage first; 50m optimal range requires closer engagement than Dreadshot; Damage Drain must be reapplied each reload cycle.
reasoning: Defining heavy weapon. 40% damage reduction at full stacks combined with class-leading damage per shot — halving enemy output while hitting hardest in class is unmatched. Gets outperformed by other category weapons like storm racks.

name: Versa
perkDesc: Has 2 firing modes, as a sniper and as a machine gun
strengths: Flexible weapon as it can perform as both a sniper and a machine gun
weaknesses: Relatively high reload, and not enough damage to outweigh that reload
reasoning: Not a bad weapon overall but gets outperformed at all ranges by alternatives. Does offer good flexibility in terms of effective range

name: Longarm
perkDesc: The farther the target is, the more damage the weapon will cause.
strengths: Deadeye scales damage with distance; 180m max range; Weaken Effect Chance at max rank.
weaknesses: Uncommon ceiling hard-caps damage vs Epic/Legendary mechs; slow fire rate; long reload with small magazine.
reasoning: Uncommon entry point. Deadeye bonus is real at 180m but the damage ceiling never climbs high enough to matter against higher-rarity mechs. Reload is also high

name: Gauss Rifle
perkDesc: Effective at most ranges and has high ammunition.
strengths: Only sniper with 0–180m full-spectrum optimal range; most sustained fire in the sniper category; 50% Double Damage Chance; available from 4 energy.
weaknesses: Rare rarity caps damage ceiling; Adaptable perk is generic; lowest per-shot damage in category by a wide margin.
reasoning: A versatile sniper — full-range optimal removes all positional constraints. High fire rate and Double Damage Chance generate reliable pressure no other sniper matches. Very lacking in terms of damage.

name: Quantum Gun
perkDesc: Fire a number of shots to apply Stasis and Weaken to a target.
strengths: 200m optimal range — longest in sniper category; Paradox applies Stasis AND Weaken simultaneously; 50% Double Damage Chance; large magazine.
weaknesses: Lowest per-shot damage in category — pure CC utility, not a damage dealer; plays nothing like a traditional sniper; reload creates gaps in CC rotations.
reasoning: CC specialist. Dual Stasis + Weaken from a single weapon at 200m is unique in the game. In coordinated play the CC window multiplies allied DPS far beyond its own raw numbers; solo it cannot threaten kills without support.

name: EM Rifle
perkDesc: This weapon is capable of Double Damage shots.
strengths: Highest single-shot damage in sniper; 40% Double Damage Chance; hitscan-level projectile speed.
weaknesses: Single-shot magazine — every miss is catastrophic; brief shot delay telegraphs the shot; minimum range dead zone against close attackers.
reasoning: Highest-skill sniper. A well-placed shot can deal enormous damage, especially when paired with orion; a double-proc can two-shot nearly anything. Nearly impossible to dodge once fired, but the brief shot delay and single-shot reload punish every miss ruthlessly. Also struggles a lot against mods

name: Tetra Rifle
perkDesc: The last bullet deals increased damage based on how many prior shots hit. Manually reloading resets the bonus. A portion of all damage bypasses Personal Shields.
strengths: Final Blow compounds 2.5× per prior hit — all 3 shots connecting makes shot 4 deal 7.5× base; shield bypass on all bullets; highest DPS/Energy of all Legendary snipers.
weaknesses: Final Blow resets on manual reload — trigger discipline mandatory; hit requirement collapses vs highly mobile targets.
reasoning: Top-tier precision sniper. With 3 prior hits the last shot does 7.5× base damage, making the full magazine among the highest-burst windows in the game. Shield bypass counters defensive compositions. Skill-gated but rewards consistent aim with S-tier output.

name: Continuum
perkDesc: Apply constant pressure to your enemies without having to reload.
strengths: Infinite magazine — never stops firing; tied with Tetra Rifle for highest DPS/Energy in sniper; 0–140m optimal range; 30% Double Damage Chance.
weaknesses: No reload rhythm for repositioning breaks; 140m max range shorter than EM Rifle and Railgun; per-shot damage lower than single-shot snipers.
reasoning: A decent weapon for sustained combat, but needs long exposure to output meaningful amounts of damage.

name: Quasher
perkDesc: Two firing modes. Sniper mode stacks hits; Enhanced mode fires homing explosive rounds equal to hits stacked. Enhanced bullets track targets and deal splash damage.
strengths: Full sniper phase generates 8 homing explosive Enhanced rounds (5.8× sniper damage each); Enhanced rounds track targets — nearly unavoidable; 30% Double Damage Chance.
weaknesses: Full sniper phase required to maximise Enhanced output; shorter range than most Legendary snipers; slow Enhanced projectiles allow cover-seeking. Enhanced mode doesn't work against Stealth Mechs
reasoning: Highest burst ceiling in the sniper category. A perfect sniper phase into maximum Enhanced homing rounds delivers damage no other sniper approaches. Enhanced mode doesn't work against Stealth Mechs so it loses most of its damage against them.

name: Railgun
perkDesc: Every hit from this weapon will devastate even the strongest Mech.
strengths: Tied with EM Rifle for highest single-shot damage in category; 165m max range; 15% Double Damage Chance.
weaknesses: Worst reload in the game after just 3 shots — lowest DPS/Energy of all Legendary snipers; slow fire rate; every miss is catastrophic.
reasoning: Extraordinary per-shot power let down by the worst reload in the game. Viable only in slow long-range siege behind hard cover — ruinous in dynamic fights.

name: Javelin Rack
perkDesc: Once locked on, this weapon can track and hit the target without manual aiming.
strengths: Auto-targeting guarantees hits; 30% Double Damage Chance; widest energy tier range in guided; blast radius absorbs variance.
weaknesses: Rare rarity caps damage; 75m max range is shortest in guided; minimum range dead zone; punishing reload after few shots.
reasoning: Entry-level guided weapon. Auto-Targeting adds no enhancement over the base class trait at Rare. Short range and long reload create dead zones — worth using only when energy can't stretch to higher rarities.

name: Cryo Javelin
perkDesc: Sustained fire applies a Stasis Effect that dramatically slows the target.
strengths: Stasis through auto-tracking missiles — target cannot sprint away from lock; 6-shot magazine applies Stasis faster than sustained-fire alternatives; 30% Double Damage Chance.
weaknesses: Only available at energy 6 and 12 — most limited tier selection of any weapon; 75m max range; longest reload in guided.
reasoning: Most reliable Stasis delivery in the game — auto-tracking ensures every tick connects regardless of target movement. Two-tier energy limitation is a real constraint, but the CC payoff justifies B-tier in team play.

name: Helix Rack
perkDesc: Superior targeting speed, range, and missile arc height.
strengths: Fastest lock-on and highest arc of any Epic guided; highest damage of any Epic guided; 90m range; 30% Double Damage Chance; full 5-tier energy availability.
weaknesses: Slow reload after few shots; minimum range gap; Epic ceiling loses to Legendary options.
reasoning: Best Epic guided option. Superior lock speed and arc height make missiles harder to evade, and 90m range opens engagements the 75m weapons can't reach. Holds its ground in Legendary-heavy lobbies.

name: Savant
perkDesc: Locks onto and damages up to 3 enemies simultaneously. Damage scales with the number of targets locked.
strengths: Scales to 225% DPS at 3 locks; highest DPS/Energy of all Legendary guided; 15% Double Damage Chance; no minimum range.
weaknesses: 80m max range — shortest of all Legendary guided; full damage scale requires 3 enemies nearby; missiles less predictable in dense cover.
reasoning: Multi-target specialist and strongest Legendary guided overall. At 3 targets it deals 225% of single-target output — more total damage per magazine than any other guided weapon. The projectiles can be inconsistent and thus not always hit.

name: Strike Rocket
perkDesc: Lock on and release projectiles manually. Change targets between shots. Magazine size scales with energy capacity.
strengths: Manual projectile release and mid-magazine target swapping — only guided weapon to split fire with full control; 110m optimal range; 30% Double Damage Chance; large blast radius.
weaknesses: Manual advantage only realised by players who actively split fire; lower per-shot damage than Savant and Disc Launcher.
reasoning: Most tactically flexible guided weapon. Splitting tracking rockets across multiple targets with manual control is unique in the category. A-tier because the advantage only matters in active play; underperforms Savant in raw single-target DPS/Energy.

name: Gemini
perkDesc: Fires two tracking rockets. The first applies Weaken; the second applies Stasis.
strengths: First rocket applies Weaken — second rocket deals 1.5× damage on the weakened target; Stasis on second rocket locks the target; 170m range — longest in guided; rockets chase targets; 30% Double Damage Chance.
weaknesses: Lowest base fire rate of any guided weapon; slow projectile speed gives enemies time to find hard cover.
reasoning: Range and CC king. Weaken-into-Stasis at 170m is a kill setup for allied snipers from positions no other guided weapon reaches. The Weaken boost means the second rocket hits for 50% more, making the two-rocket volley punch well above its listed damage. S-tier alongside Savant: Savant for multi-target sustained, Gemini for single-target CC at extreme range.

name: Disc Launcher
perkDesc: Once locked on, this weapon can track and hit the target without manual aiming.
strengths: Highest per-shot damage in guided; by far the widest blast radius in category — near-misses irrelevant; auto-tracking guarantees hits; now comparable DPS/Energy to Strike Rocket.
weaknesses: 60m optimal range — shortest of all Legendary guided; only at energy 8/12/16; Auto-Targeting perk is same as Rare Javelin Rack — no added mechanic.
reasoning: Its near impossible to deal back damage at close range. At ~713 DPS/Energy it now matches Strike Rocket and the near-10m blast radius combined with auto-tracking makes it arguably the easiest guided weapon to connect reliably. Still limited to 60m optimal range but the damage payoff within that window is decent.

name: RPG
perkDesc: Weapon deals damage in a small radius around the point of impact.
strengths: Lowest entry point in missiles at just 2 energy; 7-shot magazine; 105m max range.
weaknesses: Uncommon ceiling hard-caps damage output; Explosive is the base class mechanic with no added utility; weakest sustained output in the category.
reasoning: Budget starting missile. Fills a slot at near-zero energy cost but Explosive is just the baseline class perk with no added value. Outclassed by every other missile option the moment energy allows an upgrade.

name: Missile Rack
perkDesc: Fires a set stream of rockets, rapidly emptying the magazine into the enemy.
strengths: Longest range of any Epic missile at 150m; Alpha Strike concentrates the full magazine rapidly for burst windows; four energy tiers.
weaknesses: Heavy 10s reload after just 5 shots; rapid burst burns ammo fast with no follow-up; no CC or utility perk.
reasoning: Range specialist in the Epic tier. 150m reach opens engagements no other Epic missile can match, and Alpha Strike burst can punish exposed targets before they close distance. The 10s reload is the defining weakness — poor reload discipline turns it from a sustained threat into a burst-once weapon.

name: Voltaic RPG
perkDesc: Supercharged warheads apply a Shock effect on targets, impairing aim.
strengths: Shock Payload impairs aim on every hit — uniquely effective against precision weapon users; strong DPS/Energy for an Epic missile; fast 5.5s reload for a 6-shot magazine.
weaknesses: 90m max range is short for a missile; Epic ceiling caps raw damage; awkward energy tiers at 8/14/16 limit build flexibility.
reasoning: CC-oriented Epic missile. Shock Payload disrupts aim on every hit, making it particularly strong against sniper-heavy compositions. Best DPS/Energy among the Epics and a fast reload, but the 90m range and unusual energy tiers limit its flexibility.

name: Blast RPG
perkDesc: Missiles deal damage in a large radius around their impact point. Missiles will be attracted towards nearby enemy Mechs on their flight path.
strengths: Large blast radius absorbs near-misses; Power Play auto-attraction reduces aim demand in messy engagements; large 10-shot magazine; 120m range; now competitive DPS/Energy.
weaknesses: Power Play homing is unreliable against fast or evasive mechs; no CC or utility.
reasoning: The damage is quite weak, the homing also makes back hits more difficult, also making the radius less useful. The large blast radius and Power Play attraction remain its identity — the most forgiving Legendary missile now also hits hard enough to matter.

name: Charge Rocket
perkDesc: Fires 1–5 rockets in quick succession, depending on charge time. Reload Speed is faster if fewer rockets are fired. If 5 rockets are charged, holding the fire button will increase your aim speed. Firing all 5 rockets will grant your Mech a temporary Speed Boost.
strengths: Highest DPS/Energy in the missile category by a wide margin; Speed Boost on full release enables aggressive kite-in kite-out play; partial charge allows faster reloads when fewer rockets are needed.
weaknesses: 80m max range — shortest in the entire missile category; requires holding charge to maximise output; loses value if forced into long-range engagements.
reasoning: Category benchmark by raw output. Near-instant 5-rocket burst at 150rpm followed by a 2s total reload gives sustained DPS no other missile approaches. The Speed Boost on full release adds mobility that makes the 80m range manageable on fast mechs. S-tier through sheer damage efficiency — the range cap is the only real constraint.

name: Hornet
perkDesc: Shoots bursts of three projectiles, with a small delay between each burst. Each successful hit fills the status effect bar. When filled, the enemy is inflicted with the Venom status effect and takes Damage over time. Venom Damage bypasses Personal Mech Shields and Shield Mods.
strengths: Fires in bursts of 3; Venom DoT triggers every 5 hits — 3 procs per magazine (32,155 each) add 96,465 bonus damage — 121,200 total per cycle; Venom bypasses Personal Mech Shields and Shield Mods entirely; 110m range.
weaknesses: Venom cannot stack — firing past 5 hits before the effect expires wastes the proc; optimal play requires deliberate fire-pause rhythm that punishes aggressive repositioning; 7s reload is among the longest for Legendary missiles.
reasoning: Counter-shield specialist built around a strict fire-pause rhythm. Optimal play: dump 5 rockets, wait 2s for Venom to run, repeat twice — all 3 procs land cleanly for 121,200 total per 14.7s cycle. Continuous spray at 212 rpm causes the second proc to overlap and be lost, dropping output to 88k. The 2s Venom window fits neatly inside the 7s reload after the final group, so no time is wasted.

name: Disruptor
perkDesc: Each shot deals Path Damage during flight and Splash Damage on impact.
strengths: Devastation deals damage along the entire flight path — hits grouped enemies multiple times; 7m path radius and 7m splash radius punish packed formations; 0.3s path damage timer adds lingering area.
weaknesses: Lowest DPS/Energy of any Legendary missile; single-shot magazine demands a reload every 5.5s; path damage only relevant against stationary or grouped targets.
reasoning: Niche formation punisher. Devastation is uniquely powerful when the flight path intersects multiple clustered enemies — path damage effectively multiplies per-shot value. Against isolated mobile targets, however, it is simply the lowest-DPS Legendary missile with a punishing single-shot reload rhythm.

name: Storm Rack
perkDesc: Fires a stream of missiles that deal extra Damage to most enemy Shields.
strengths: Longest optimal range in the missile category at 160m; Shieldbreaker +50% damage to shields crushes defensive setups; highest DPM of any Legendary missile.
weaknesses: Heaviest reload in the category at 11s; Shieldbreaker loses value against shield-free builds; missed salvos create long dead windows.
reasoning: Anti-shield range anchor. 160m reach enables safe standoff fire no other missile can match, and +50% shield damage makes it the definitive counter to heavy shield builds. The 11s reload is brutal but the legendary reload implant cuts that in half.

name: Autocannon
perkDesc: Effective at most ranges and has high ammunition.
strengths: Extremely energy-efficient; high ammo count; consistent sustained fire at all engagement ranges.
weaknesses: Low damage ceiling; outscaled quickly by Rare and above; Common rarity limits maximum potential.
reasoning: The Autocannon is the reliable starter weapon for tight-energy builds. Adaptable keeps it useful at various ranges but raw damage falls off hard. Worth using as a 2-energy filler — nothing more.

name: Plasma Cannon
perkDesc: This weapon favors lots of damage in a short time over long firefights.
strengths: Flash Fire burst timing rewards aggressive play; decent accuracy per shot.
weaknesses: Shortest max range of all assault weapons (75m); slowest fire rate; 25-shot mag punishes every missed shot.
reasoning: Flash Fire sounds strong but the slow fire rate and tiny magazine mean burst potential is mostly theoretical. The 75m range ceiling is severely limiting. Better options exist at every energy tier.

name: Pulse Cannon
perkDesc: A large magazine means this weapon is nearly always ready for action.
strengths: High fire rate; 90-round magazine minimises downtime; solid 60m optimal range for sustained pressure.
weaknesses: Hit cone widens at higher ranks; no special damage multiplier; damage per shot is lower than burst-style weapons.
reasoning: High Ammo keeps you in the fight longer than most assault weapons. High fire rate with a large magazine means consistent pressure with minimal downtime. Lacks in damage and gets obsolete in early game itself.

name: Fusion Cannon
perkDesc: Fires rapidly, dealing high damage at medium range.
strengths: High damage per shot; Fusillade enables strong DPS windows; available across 5 energy tiers for flexibility.
weaknesses: Lowest fire rate in the assault family; small magazine; punishing reload on misses.
reasoning: The Fusion Cannon punches hard per shot and Fusillade amplifies that in close-medium engagements. Available from 6 to 16 energy makes it very flexible across mech builds. The low fire rate and small mag demand precision — high reward for accurate players.

name: Viper
perkDesc: Deals consistent damage with bullets and fires an extra powerful Rocket after every 8th shot. Once locked on, the Rocket can track and hit targets without manual aiming.
strengths: Longest optimal range (90m) of all assault weapons; dual bullet+rocket damage; Finisher rockets auto-track targets; effective at all ranges.
weaknesses: Moderate fire rate; rocket tracking requires a brief lock-on window to activate.
reasoning: The Viper is a relatively decent assault weapon. Finisher fires a homing rocket every 8 shots, giving guaranteed bonus damage on top of consistent bullet DPS. The 90m optimal range outranges nearly every other assault weapon. Overshadowed heavily by Overdriver which is almost always the better pick between the two

name: Overdriver
perkDesc: Deals more Damage the longer it shoots. Can fire at a high rate without reloading, unless pushed beyond its limits and burns out.
strengths: Highest fire rate of all assault weapons; no reload needed — heat management replaces reload; first burst ramps from 1× to 2×, then each cycle stays in the bonus zone (25–95% heat) for sustained peak output.
weaknesses: Cold start costs a full ramp-up burst before settling into optimal rhythm; burns out instantly if heat exceeds 95%.
reasoning: Optimal play: fire to 95% heat, stop and let it cool to the lower bonus threshold (~25%), then fire again — never reloading. The diagram shows the cold-start ramp, followed by repeated bonus-zone bursts with passive cooldown gaps.

name: Oracle
perkDesc: When 25% of the Magazine has been fired, a Drone deploys and also fires at the target. Drone bullets apply the Reveal effect, making targets visible through walls until destroyed.
strengths: Longest max range (140m) of all assault weapons; Reveal effect provides team-wide intel; drone doubles effective output mid-magazine.
weaknesses: Drone only activates at 35% mag threshold — useless in short engagements; DPS split between gun and drone makes raw output underwhelming solo.
reasoning: The Oracle is a unique hybrid — weapon and utility tool in one. Tracking Shot is powerful when active but conditional, making it inconsistent in quick fights. The 140m range and Reveal effect shine in coordinated play

name: Berserker
perkDesc: Firing increases bullet dispersion. However, each bullet's Crit Chance steadily increases until the end of the Magazine, up to 100%.
strengths: 100% crit chance at end of magazine is enormous; large 80-round mag gives long crit ramp window; 30% double damage chance stacks on top.
weaknesses: Bullet dispersion grows as crit chance climbs — late-mag accuracy is poor at range; longest reload of any assault weapon.
reasoning: High-risk, high-reward. Crit ramp to 100% is devastating on paper but spread grows simultaneously, undermining accuracy at distance. Best in close-range brawls where spread is irrelevant. The long reload demands you finish fights fast.

name: Reaver
perkDesc: High Damage and Rate of Fire plus fast Reload Speed make Reaver consistently deadly at mid-range or closer.
strengths: Fastest reload in the assault category — nearly zero downtime; 70% Double Damage Chance; high fire rate with strong base damage.
weaknesses: Very short max range (60m) limits usefulness at distance; only 15 rounds per magazine before reload cycle.
reasoning: The Reaver is a close-range monster. The 1-second reload means you are effectively always firing, and 70% double damage chance makes every volley explosive. The 60m range cap is the only real limiter — pair it with a fast mech and it dominates every close-quarters fight.

name: Carbine
perkDesc: Fires short bursts of high-damage, high-velocity rounds.
strengths: High-velocity projectiles (160 speed); 120m max range offers flexible positioning; burst pattern rewards precise aim.
weaknesses: Only 30m optimal range — extremely tight engagement window; below-average fire rate; only available at energy 8+.
reasoning: The Carbine is a specialist weapon for aggressive mechs that close distance fast. Lacks heavily in damage.

name: Thermal Lance
perkDesc: Sustained fire applies a Weaken Effect that increases the damage the target takes.
strengths: Cheapest beam at 2 energy; Scorcher Weaken amplifies all allied damage on target; long fire window keeps Weaken applied continuously.
weaknesses: Lowest dmgPerEnergy of all beams — 38.9s cycle (16.4s fire + 22.5s reload) devastates sustained efficiency; Rare rarity hard-caps its ceiling.
reasoning: The entry-level beam. Scorcher is a useful debuff but the reload-heavy cycle keeps sustained output at the floor of the category. Worth using only as a filler in a tight 2-energy slot.

name: Stasis Beam
perkDesc: Sustained fire applies a Stasis Effect that dramatically slows the target.
strengths: Stasis dramatically slows targets — strong CC; long fire window keeps Stasis locked; longest max range of all beams at 150m.
weaknesses: Second-lowest dmgPerEnergy in category — 34.9s cycle (14.9s fire + 20s reload) is punishing; high energy floor (8 minimum); Stasis requires sustained fire to apply.
reasoning: A CC anchor rather than a damage dealer. The long fire window is ideal for maintaining Stasis but the reload-heavy cycle tanks sustained efficiency.

name: Burrow Beam
perkDesc: Fires a straight, continuous beam which passes through Mechs. Has a single charge in its Magazine, which reloads when empty. The beam cannot pass through objects, walls or any environmental obstructions.
strengths: Piercing Laser hits every mech in a line for full damage — real output multiplies in group fights; +6.82% damage per shot partially offsets reload nerf.
weaknesses: Beam cannot penetrate walls or objects; 80m max range is the second shortest of all Legendary beams; 70% of damage dealt to Shields rather than HP — less effective against shield-depleted targets; longer 13.3s cycle (7.8s fire + 4.5s reload + 1s delay).
reasoning: Heavy Damage and a moderate range. Reload is mid but with the correct implant setups its one of the best weapons in the game.

name: Graviton Beam
perkDesc: Firing at a target builds up a devastating Implosion Effect.
strengths: Highest in-beam DPS of all beams; 5 Implosion procs per magazine (44,625 each) add 223,125 bonus damage — 285,600 total per cycle; 100m range.
weaknesses: Highest energy floor in category (10 minimum); Implosion requires sustained on-target fire — repositioning resets buildup.
reasoning: The Implosion procs are the real story — 5 guaranteed 44,625-damage bursts per magazine on top of 62,475 base equals 285,600 total damage per 36.5s cycle. Against mods the implosions hit those instead and make the damage quite bad as compared to its alternatives.

name: Particle Beam
perkDesc: Deal Damage in Beam Mode to charge up a powerful Blast.
strengths: Short 5.8s cycle (3.8s fire + 2s reload) drives strong sustained efficiency; Ionic Charge blast reaches 200m — furthest range of all beams; rapid cycling maintains constant pressure.
weaknesses: Ionic Charge blast requires disciplined charge-fire rhythm; beam-only output without landing the blast is below potential; short window demands consistent aim.
reasoning: The 5.8s cycle drives solid sustained Damage Per Energy. The 200m Ionic Charge blast is the longest-range attack in the beam category. Its range advantage is unmatched.

name: Compound Beam
perkDesc: Has two firing modes. Deal damage in Beam Mode to apply Stasis to enemies and charge up the Pulse Mode. When ready, Pulse Mode emits a fan-shaped blast that deals increased Damage and applies a short EMP effect.
strengths: Highest sustained dmgPerEnergy of all beams; tightest cycle in category at 3.8s (2.3s fire + 1.5s reload); beam applies Stasis while charging the EMP fan-blast — dual-status combo is unmatched.
weaknesses: Shortest range of all Legendary beams at 50m — demands close engagement; dual-mode rhythm requires practice; both effects require landing the correct mode.
reasoning: Top sustained efficiency in the beam category. The 3.8s cycle maximises damage uptime and the Stasis-into-EMP combo controls entire groups simultaneously. Short range is the only real constraint — pair with a fast mech to stay inside 50m.
